thread_analysis.thread_summary: OM Digital Solutions (contact Tadashi Horiuchi, OMDS, formerly under Olympus) works with Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Toshitaka Mochizuki) on Bluetooth SIG certification for an HFP-implementing headset product. The thread documents an extended, ultimately unresolved HFP PTS test troubleshooting saga (DUT not discoverable, Paging connection failures) that led to escalating to an in-person lab session, a pivotal decision to abandon active Profile testing entirely in favor of referencing a currently active Profile Subsystem QDID (discovered via researching Infineon's post-Cypress-acquisition AIROC SDK rebrand) to achieve HFP test exemption, an ICS Mandatory-item clarification, an order/billing adjustment question, two Review Page correction questions (an unnecessary-seeming SPP inclusion explained as an HFP dependency, and an outdated company name/address sourced from the account database), and final Compliance Folder document scope questions (public disclosure status, design document reuse for the operation manual, and a module-datasheet substitute for antenna documentation) before final Compliance Folder delivery (March 2026).
all_questions_found: Why isn't the DUT discoverable/connectable during HFP PTS testing, and how can this be resolved? (see thread_0234_case_01)
Does an ICS item marked Mandatory (Status M) really have to be set to YES? (see thread_0234_case_02)
Can HFP PTS testing be avoided by referencing a currently active Profile Subsystem QDID, given the prior exemption-providing QDID is now deprecated? (see thread_0234_case_03)
How should the order/billing be adjusted after canceling the Profile testing portion mid-engagement? (see thread_0234_case_04)
Why does the registration include SPP when the product doesn't separately implement it? (see thread_0234_case_05)
Why does the Review Page show an outdated company name/address, and can it be corrected? (see thread_0234_case_06)
Are the Compliance Folder documents public, can existing design documents be reused, and can a module datasheet substitute for dedicated antenna documentation? (see thread_0234_case_07)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread spans the full registration lifecycle for a profile-testing-troubled product: an unresolved DUT discoverability/Paging failure during HFP PTS testing that escalated to an in-person lab session, a successful pivot to a test-exemption strategy via locating a currently active Profile Subsystem QDID under a vendor's rebranded SDK lineage, ICS Mandatory-item semantics, Review Page verification catching both a legitimate specification-dependency question (SPP/HFP) and a genuine account-data error (outdated company name), and pragmatic Compliance Folder document substitutions (existing design document reuse, module datasheet excerpt) when original developer documentation wasn't fully available.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Across this thread, Allion consistently favored proportionate, evidence-based resolutions: escalating only to in-person troubleshooting once remote methods were exhausted, actively researching for a currently valid test-exemption alternative rather than assuming testing was now mandatory, correctly distinguishing specification dependencies (SPP/HFP) from registration errors, and accepting substantively equivalent existing documentation for Compliance Folder requirements rather than insisting on newly authored materials.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0234_case_01 through thread_0234_case_07 for the specific risks of each question.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — the team's research into the Infineon AIROC Profile Subsystem alternative avoided what could have become a costly, unresolved firmware-debugging detour, and the Review Page review caught a genuine data error (outdated company name) that the customer might not have otherwise noticed since it doesn't appear on the public page.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When PTS test troubleshooting stalls after multiple remote rounds, actively search for an alternative test-exemption path (e.g., a currently valid Profile Subsystem QDID, even one requiring research into a vendor's corporate/SDK history) before continuing to sink time into firmware-level debugging, and always carefully review Review Page content for both specification-dependency questions and genuine account-data errors before Submission, since some account-sourced fields (like company name) don't appear on the public page and can go unnoticed across multiple registrations.
